issues.description: The problem statement requires that the function 'start_app' be the global entry point, but the template defines 'global main' and provides a 'main' label (no 'start_app'). The solution defines a 'start_app' label but does not declare it global; it still declares 'global main'. This inconsistency about which symbol must be global (start_app vs main) will confuse students about the required entry point and may prevent them from making the correct symbol global as the spec requires.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the entrypoint consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update template and solution to use 'start_app' as the global entrypoint: replace or add 'global start_app' (and remove or adjust 'global main'), ensure a 'start_app' label exists and contains/dispatches the program entry logic; or (B) change the problem statement to require 'main' as the global entrypoint if that was intended. Prefer option A to match the current problem text: add 'global start_app' to both template_repository/helloWorld.asm and solution_repository/helloWorld.asm (and provide a start_app stub in the template) so students clearly see and can implement the required global symbol.

issues.description: The problem statement requires the function 'start_app' to be the global entry point, but the template declares 'global main' and provides a 'main' label. The solution file defines a 'start_app' label but does not declare it as global (and still leaves 'global main'). This mismatch across artifacts prevents students from clearly mapping the described entry-point requirement (start_app) to the provided starter code and the reference solution, creating confusion about which symbol should be the program's global entry point.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the entry-point identifier consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fixes (choose one):
1) Align code to the problem statement: in both template_repository/helloWorld.asm and solution_repository/helloWorld.asm replace or add the global directive for the described entry point (e.g., change 'global main' to 'global start_app' and rename the 'main' label to 'start_app' or ensure a single 'start_app' label exists and is declared global).
2) Or adjust the problem statement to require 'main' as the global entry point instead of 'start_app' if 'main' is the intended symbol. 
Either approach will remove the naming mismatch and let students unambiguously map the problem requirement to the starter code and reference solution.
